reason: Different facts of the same 11 July 1944 US offensive on Saint-Lô: C0801 (CMH, Lexikon, R588/R180) is the division sector east and north-east of Saint-Lô; C8410 (FMS B-541, R853) is the local penetration at Saint-Georges-d'Elle sealed off that day; kept side by side (B-541 is also cited on C0801).
Two different places taken by the 43rd Division about 3 March 1945: Ellis (C1500) has Calcar secured; Stacey (C7544, p. 514) has the 214th Brigade occupying Kehrum on the 3rd.
Two separate landings of the 4th Special Service Brigade on 1 November 1944: the main body at Westkapelle (Infatuate II) and No. 4 Commando at Flushing (Infatuate I) (Stacey pp. 414-16).

Different actions on 31 October 1944 by different parts of the 2nd Canadian Infantry Division: the Royal Regiment clears the east end of the Walcheren causeway (Stacey p. 404) while a squadron of the 8th Reconnaissance Regiment overruns North Beveland (p. 404).

Two accounts of the same 9th Panzer Division counterattack on Lindern on 30 November 1944 that disagree on the outcome: B-811 (C8048, R820) has Lindern retaken, B-367 (C8169, R824) has the assault parties entering but not holding; same family (FMS), kept side by side pending roadmap 282.

Two command posts of II Fliegerkorps in one period (FMS B-509): the corps headquarters at Compiègne (C8284) and the advanced command post at St. Piat [?] for the 7th Army (C8285), both dated 6 June 1944 for the 6-28 June period.
Two different places taken by the 5th Parachute Division on 20 December 1944 (FMS B-023, German p.29): Regiment 14 takes the Nothum crossroads and two engineer companies take Wiltz.

Two command-post moves of the Seventh Army on the same day, 7 September 1944 (FMS B-730, R856, typed p.-33- and -34-): to Chaudfontaine, then after US tanks arrived at 17:30 on to Limbourg; different actions of one kind on the same day.
